summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as LLM-powered applications scale into production, where opaque model behavior, hallucinations, and consumption-based pricing can quickly erode reliability and budgets. Observability tools provide tracing, evaluation, and cost tracking so teams can monitor prompts, debug workflows, and optimize spend. New Relic reports 30% quarter-over-quarter growth in AI monitoring adoption, underscoring how critical visibility has become for shipping trustworthy AI systems.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: Prompt/LLM traces, chains, agent workflows, evaluation results, and latency across LangChain and non-LangChain apps.
features: End-to-end trace and span visibility for chains and agents
Built-in dataset management and offline/online evaluations
Deep native integration with the LangChain ecosystem
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month with overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention. At 100,000 traces, LangSmith Plus runs approximately $264/month.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain/LangGraph who want tightly integrated tracing and evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, per-model costs, latency, usage by user/department, and caching — operating as a lightweight proxy/gateway.
features: One-line base URL change for instant integration
Cost computation across 300+ models via model-cost repository
Request logging, caching, and rate limiting
tools.pricing: Free tier at 10,000 requests/month with usage-based pricing thereafter; Helicone Pro reportedly reaches the 100,000-trace milestone at around $79/month (per Markaicode).
tools.best_for: Teams wanting near-instant, low-overhead cost tracking and governance without framework lock-in.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiments, model evaluations, and production application quality alongside traditional ML experiment tracking.
features: W&B Weave for LLM app tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; team and enterprise plans are consumption/seat-based with custom enterprise pricing for larger deployments.
tools.best_for: ML teams who want unified experiment tracking and LLM observability in a single mature platform.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM and ML model performance, embeddings/drift, RAG quality, and evaluations with OpenTelemetry-based tracing.
features: Open-source Arize Phoenix for tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open source; the managed Arize AI platform offers free/startup tiers with enterprise pricing for production scale.
tools.best_for: Teams needing open, standards-based (OpenTelemetry) observability with strong RAG and drift analysis.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token/cost tracking, online evaluations, and user feedback across any framework.
features: Cost and token tracking per trace
tools.pricing: Open-source and free to self-host; managed cloud offers a free Hobby tier with Pro and enterprise plans priced by usage/seats.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable alternative with full data control and flexible integration.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, traces, and metrics exported via OpenTelemetry to existing observability backends.
features: Vendor-neutral export to any OTel-compatible backend
Automatic instrumentation of popular LLM SDKs
Integrates with existing enterprise observability stacks
tools.pricing: Free and open source (SDK/instrumentation); costs come from whatever observability backend you export data to.
tools.best_for: Teams standardizing on OpenTelemetry who want to pipe LLM telemetry into existing dashboards without vendor lock-in.

cost_tips: Use a gateway/proxy (like Helicone) to meter and attribute spend per user, team, or feature so you can identify and cut the most expensive usage.
Cache repeated or similar requests and reuse responses to avoid paying for duplicate inference calls.
Route tasks to the cheapest capable model — use smaller/faster models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning.
Trim prompts and context windows, and track token usage per trace to eliminate wasted tokens and oversized system prompts.
